standardHealthChecks.name: Liquidity Health
standardHealthChecks.description: The current ratio stands at 0.64 (Current Assets of LKR 27.8B vs. Current Liabilities of LKR 43.7B). While working capital deficits are common in retail supermarket models due to fast inventory turnover and trade payables, the heavy reliance on bank overdrafts (LKR 11.81B against LKR 1.54B cash) presents liquidity exposure.

standardHealthChecks.name: Profitability Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Total revenue expanded by 18% YoY to LKR 50.78B, with gross profit rising 17% to LKR 6.61B. Operating profit (EBIT) grew 18% to LKR 2.75B (5.4% EBIT margin). Net profit slipped slightly by 3% to LKR 1.06B due to a 45% increase in tax expense, but annualized ROE remains solid at ~18.8%.

standardHealthChecks.name: Debt Management
standardHealthChecks.description: Total interest-bearing debt (excluding lease liabilities) is LKR 20.71B, resulting in a Debt-to-Equity ratio of 91.7% (or 151.6% including lease liabilities). Interest coverage ratio is healthy at approximately 3.68x (EBIT of LKR 2.75B vs Finance Costs of LKR 0.75B).

standardHealthChecks.name: Cash Flow Health
standardHealthChecks.description: Operating cash flow grew significantly by 33.4% YoY to LKR 4.77B for the quarter. Free cash flow generation remains strong at LKR 2.83B after accounting for property, plant, equipment, and intangible capex.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Inventory Efficiency & Turnover
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Inventory decreased from LKR 18.51B as of March 2026 to LKR 17.21B as of June 2026, despite an 18% increase in sales volume. Annualized inventory turnover is ~9.9x (~37 days), reflecting tight working capital control across FMCG and Supermarket retail operations.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: In food manufacturing and supermarket retail, fast inventory turnover is essential to prevent inventory spoilage, minimize holding costs, and maximize working capital efficiency.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Segment Performance & Revenue Diversification
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Both core operating segments delivered robust top-line growth: Supermarket retail revenue grew 16% YoY to LKR 40.92B (operating profit LKR 1.76B), while Manufacturing expanded 23% YoY to LKR 9.86B with strong operating profitability (LKR 3.06B, 29.7% segment margin).
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: Analyzing business segment contribution is crucial for a dual-business company to evaluate whether high-margin manufacturing balances high-volume, low-margin retail.

dynamicHealthChecks.name: Bank Overdraft & Short-Term Debt Exposure
dynamicHealthChecks.description: Bank overdrafts grew to LKR 11.81B, forming over 27% of current liabilities. Net short-term debt and overdraft pressure raised total net finance expenses by 26% YoY to LKR 727.8 million.
dynamicHealthChecks.relevanceReason: For retail chains with thin net margins (~2.1%), unhedged short-term floating debt and high overdraft balances can rapidly erode bottom-line profitability during elevated interest rate environments.

recommendations: Refinance a portion of the short-term bank overdraft balance (LKR 11.81B) into structured longer-term facilities to improve the current ratio and mitigate re-pricing risk.
Optimize finance expenses by using the strong quarterly operating cash flow (LKR 4.77B) to directly pay down expensive short-term interest-bearing debt.
Focus on improving margin realization in the Supermarket segment (currently ~4.2% operating margin) through private label expansion and supply chain efficiencies.
Evaluate tax strategy and deferred tax planning to cushion against elevated corporate tax charges, which surged 45% YoY in the current period.
result.analysisNotes: Ceylon Cold Stores PLC exhibits strong operational health, driven by solid top-line revenue expansion (+18% YoY) across both FMCG manufacturing and Supermarket retail. Operating cash flow generation (+33% YoY) and inventory turnover remain strong. The primary area requiring management attention is short-term liquidity structure and bank overdraft dependence, which created a working capital deficit and pushed net finance costs up by 26%.
